news.headline: Brent crude extended to about $117.30 a barrel, a new multi-year high, on fears the US-Iran war resumes.
Trump said the US "may do another little Epic Fury" and will "have Iran finished very soon," hinting at new strikes.
Nasdaq closed -0.21% and S&P -0.52%, both down for a 2nd straight week; Dow fell 654 points (-1.24%).
Iran threatened strikes on Gulf oil, data center and AI infrastructure if attacked again.
Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure continued, keeping US oil above $100.
Fed meets Wednesday; markets price only ~5% odds of a hike, but ~80% for December.
Nasdaq-100 fell about 1% this week, but Q3 earnings are tracking ~45% growth after mega-cap beats.
10-year yield edged up to ~4.99%, staying under 5% after Thursday's big drop.
UMich sentiment at 48.0, second-lowest on record; 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%.
VIX rose 3.6% to 19.72 into next week's earnings and Fed cluster.
Nasdaq tries to bounce after its worst day since June; still on pace for a 2nd straight weekly loss
Meta fell ~7% after raising its 2026 capex floor to $135-145B, dragging chips and AI names
10-yr yield back under 5% (~4.99%) after its biggest one-day drop in 2+ years
Oil near a 5-month high on Middle East tension: Brent ~$112, WTI ~$102
Odds of a Fed hike at next week's meeting fall to ~5% (from 37% at end of September)
VIX up ~3% to 19.6; Dow lower, S&P roughly flat
AmEx -3% on revenue miss, plans ~5% job cuts
SpaceX reportedly eyeing ~80k US cell sites: Crown Castle +7%, AT&T/Verizon/T-Mobile lower
Cybersecurity rallied 5-7% (PANW, NET) on a strong budget survey; airlines fell 4%+ on fuel costs.
Apple briefly passed Nvidia in market value (~$5.1T each) before Nvidia took the lead back.

takeaway: Weekend gap risk is the main issue: Brent near war highs (~$117) with Trump hinting at new Iran strikes and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites, which leans risk-off for NQ at Sunday's 6 PM open. Then the week turns on FOMC Wed 2 PM, MSFT/GOOGL that night, and GDP/PCE plus AMZN Thursday.
